[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Replace Non-Coprime Numbers in Array** [LC 2197 · Replace Non-Coprime Numbers in Array](https://leetcode.com/problems/replace-non-coprime-numbers-in-array/){difficulty="Hard"}

Merging is *associative along a run*: if $a,b$ share a factor and $b,c$ share a factor, the
whole stretch $a,b,c$ ends up as $\mathrm{lcm}(a,b,c)$ no matter how you bracket it, because
$\mathrm{lcm}$ absorbs prime powers monotonically. So the answer is just "maximal runs of
pairwise-connected elements, each replaced by its LCM". A left-to-right **stack** finds those
runs in one pass: push each number, and while the top shares a factor with the incoming
number, pop and fold the LCM back - the running LCM keeps growing so it will absorb the whole
run. This is the pigeonhole view of @sec-gcd-a6: an element can only be absorbed a bounded
number of times (its prime-power content is capped), so the stack work is near-linear.

[Solved in full in @sec-gcd-p5-merge.]{.card-link}

:::
